commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.name: morning

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: pptx

Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Fixed. The change is in `server/agent/github-app.ts`:

- **`server/agent/github-app.ts:24`** — `import { ArtifactGenerator, RubricScore } from './artifact-generator';`
- **`server/agent/github-app.ts:1117`** — `rubricScores: emptyArray<RubricScore>(),`

**The cause:** `emptyArray<T>()` in `shared/type-bridge.ts:91` has no inference site — no parameters, no contextual type, because `runReport` is an unannotated `const` whose type is only checked later when it's passed at line 1147. With nothing to infer from, `T` falls back to `unknown`, so the call returned `unknown[]`. `GateDecision.rubricScores` (`artifact-generator.ts:45`) requires `RubricScore[]`, and `unknown[]` is not assignable to it — that single field mismatch is what surfaced as TS2345 against the whole object literal at the call site. Supplying the type argument gives the helper the type it was designed to be told.

I walked the remaining fields of the literal against `AgentRunReport` and found no other mismatch: `finishedAt: string` satisfies `string | null`, the `as const` literals land inside their unions, `recommendations: []` and `patches: []` widen from `never[]` to their targets, and `issues` comes off `auditResult: any` so it type-checks as `any`. Excess-property checking doesn't apply, since freshness is lost when the literal is bound to `runReport` before being passed.

**One thing I could not do: run the verification command.** `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` requires approval on this host and no approver is present, and the language-server diagnostics tool was likewise not granted. So the fix above rests on reading the types, not on a compiler run — please run the typecheck to confirm before treating it as proven.

Two incidental notes:

- The pre-tool routing gate blocked all edits until a routing request existed; I wrote `build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json` using the exact recovery the hook itself specified. Remove it if your close process doesn't sweep it up.
- Unrelated to the type error, but visible while reading: the `issues` objects built at lines 1118–1125 have shape `{id, type, severity, message, location, suggestion}`, while the `Issue` interface is `{severity, category, description, location?, suggestedFix?}`. Because `auditResult` is `any`, the compiler can't see this, but `buildGateReport` and the markdown generators read `issue.category` and `issue.description` — those will be `undefined` at runtime. I left it alone as outside this task's scope.
